reviewer: Independent AI tester · experienced deck tinkerer
method: Actual shared-browser incognito tabs. Read lobby/guide/builder and public localTable DTO. All actions through rendered DOM buttons/input/change events. Setup and later encounters manually reasoned; bounded DOM heuristics handled early routine decisions. No engine/worker choice injection, private-state inspection or app changes. This is an AI qualitative review, not a human study or a controlled deck-strength experiment.

findings.finding: Hard-matchup labels do not explain threats or suggest a learning/tuning hypothesis.
findings.suggestion: Add short opponent threat notes and one small, legal example swap with tradeoffs, clearly marked as an unbenchmarked custom variant.

findings.finding: Aircheck inspector footer displayed 'Art by Mia Siergiejew · System Gateway #18' despite Aircheck beingVantage36018. Correct ability text was shown.

findings.evidence: Read card from Aircheck play options in follow-up round10.

findings.finding: Learning suggestions name pairings but do not offer an apply/open-in-lobby or tune action.
findings.suggestion: Add use-this-pairing and tune-from-this-list links; preserve exact source deck names and warn custom variants lack measurements.
findings.caveat: The targetblank popup was not surfaced by the shared tool after DOM click; I opened a new tab at the observed href. This is an automation limitation, not a verified browser defect.

findings.finding: Wrong-type boosters and boosts during movement/turn-start still appear among defaults.
findings.suggestion: Keep them behind an explicit all-abilities disclosure while emphasizing currently matching breaker actions.
findings.caveat: My initial wrong-type boosts were a heuristic error. Their visibility is a usability concern, not evidence of incorrect rules.

findings.suggestion: Add a Hiram hardware/peek lesson and resource/rig sequencing example.

ratings.scale: Subjective AI review,10=clear,polished and useful for this task; outcomes do not determine ratings.

conclusion: Useful for choosing a named pairing, weaker at helping a player explain and tune a bad pairing. Deck editing/saving/play worked. Both games completed naturally with0diagnostics, but tester strategy materially confounded the losses.
